column3: Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew calls the leaders “corners” of the people and describes the men as “drawing a sword.” BSB renders these as “leaders” and “armed with swords.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew repeats “against me” in describing their rising and surrounding the house; BSB states it once.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew asks for “a word and counsel” here; BSB renders this as “advice and verdict” and adds “now.”
The Hebrew separately negates going to one’s tent and turning aside to one’s house. BSB combines both destinations under one return verb.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew calls those receiving provisions “the people”; BSB identifies them as “the army.” It speaks of doing according to the outrage, where BSB explicitly says “to punish them.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew refers to the “tribes of Benjamin” in the plural; BSB uses the singular “tribe of Benjamin.”
The Hebrew calls the offenders “sons of worthlessness” and explicitly calls the Israelites the Benjamites’ “brothers.” BSB uses “wicked men” and “fellow Israelites.”
The Hebrew explicitly names “the sons of Benjamin”; BSB uses “they.”
The Hebrew says the men were counted, repeating the counting verb for the seven hundred. BSB uses “mobilized” and omits the repeated verb.
The Hebrew calls them “all this people” rather than “all these soldiers.” Its expression for left-handedness refers explicitly to the right hand.
The Hebrew says the men were counted and calls each “a man of war.” BSB uses “mobilized” and adds the qualification “experienced.”
The Hebrew asks who will go up “for us” first; BSB says “Who of us”.
The Hebrew says they rose “in the morning”; BSB explicitly says “the next morning.”
The Hebrew repeats “the men of Israel” as the subject of taking battle positions; BSB combines the actions under one subject.
The Hebrew says the men were destroyed “to the ground”; BSB says “on the battlefield.”
The Hebrew calls the subject “the people, the men of Israel”; BSB renders this as “the Israelite army.”

The Hebrew explicitly names “the sons of Israel” and repeats the LORD’s name three times; BSB uses “they” and replaces one occurrence with “Him.” The question uses singular “I” and “my brother,” where BSB uses plural forms.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly says “on the second day” and “to the ground”; BSB says “that same day” and leaves the ground image implicit.
The Hebrew says “all the sons of Israel and all the people” and uses separate verbs for weeping and sitting. BSB says “the Israelites, all the people” and combines these actions as “sat weeping.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew’s question uses singular “I” and “my brother,” and the LORD’s answer literally commands “go up.” BSB uses “we” and “our brothers,” then renders the command as “Fight.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
